title: Europe’s Public Investment Boom Changes Shape
text:
Europe’s Public Investment Boom Changes Shape

August Gudmundsson

Gavekal Research | 11 Aug 2026

The European Union’s post-Covid investment program is approaching its end. Known formally as NextGenerationEU, it was launched after the Covid crisis to fund investment and economic reform. At first glance, its expiry threatens an investment cliff, particularly in Southern and Eastern Europe, the program’s main beneficiaries (see Europe’s Use-It-Or-Lose-It Moment). Yet EU government investment is expected to stay close to 4% of GDP in 2027. This apparent stability masks a rotation from civilian to defense investment and a geographical shift in the marginal investment impulse toward Germany and Northern Europe.The main vehicle for NextGenerationEU is the Recovery and Resilience Facility, which accounts for roughly 90% of the program’s funds. Of the €575bn earmarked for spending, around €310bn had been recorded by the end of 2025. These funds drove roughly 40% of the rise in government gross fixed capital formation—the acquisition less disposal of fixed assets such as buildings, machinery, transport equipment and software—from €469bn to €727bn between 2021 and 2025. The surge was concentrated in Southern and Eastern Europe, which generated 86% of the rise despite accounting for just 37% of EU GDP.
